title: TLS, DNS: add dissection of Encrypted Client Hello

notes.body: Example:[ech.pcapng](/uploads/5dedbf2de2f1d100b08d9c544df42768/ech.pcapng)

The current approach has as unfortunate side-effect that the field names start with `dns.` instead of `tls.`.

What about passing the ett and hf IDs as parameters to the function? We could possibly share the underlying `value_string` mappings.

Hi @Lekensteyn, thanks for your review!\
Just to be sure: do you want to have duplicate fields? Something like "dns.hpke.key_config.cipher_suite.kdf_id" and  "tls.hpke.key_config.cipher_suite.kdf_id"?

[BTW, we have the same issue, but bigger, in dissection of the CH extension for EncryptedExtensions since we need to duplicate all the fields of "ECHConfigList"...]

Good point about ECHConfig. Since ECH is a TLS extension, I think we should probably move all of the dissection functionality in there and have the DNS dissector reference this.

Another idea is to call a new `tls-ech` or `tls-echconfig` dissector with the ECHConfig payload, and leave it as opaque blob to the DNS dissector.

At some point we might want to have the HTTP dissector call this dissector for a potential `/.well-known/` endpoint, e.g. https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-tls-wkech/, so creating a dissector would naturally fit in that.

It would probably be best to keep it as closely integrated with the TLS dissector as possible, in case we want to implement decryption of ECH-enabled handshakes. It would not be a requirement though, we can simply dissect the same data twice. Once for visual dissection, and once again for extracting the data required for decryption.

```suggestion:-0+0
              cur_offset += call_dissector(tls_echconfig_handle, next_tvb, pinfo, svcb_param_tree);
```

This will trip on a `DISSECTOR_ASSERT` if `tls_echconfig_handle` is NULL. I *think* we should be okay since the TLS dissector cannot be disabled, and this has nothing to do with "Disabled Protocols".

@Lekensteyn, out of curiosity, what do you mean with "TLS dissector cannot be disabled"? Is there another level of "disabling protocols" other than the one that the user can change in "Analyze -> Disabled Protocols" window?

No that is exactly the one I was thinking of. What I meant was that the dissectors will always be registered in code even if `call_dissector` will end up doing nothing due to `proto_is_protocol_enabled` returning FALSE in `call_dissector_work`.

Use of `ssl_add_vector` and `ssl_end_vector` is probably nicer to avoid accidental integer/buffer overflows for TLS vector structures like `HpkeSymmetricCipherSuite cipher_suites<4..2^16-4>`. It also adds nicer diagnostics if implementations have bugs that needs to be caught.

In this case it doesn't really matter because you are operating on a 16-bit unsigned integer length.
Feel free to apply it if you think it is helpful, otherwise feel free to leave this for later.

Can we use `ssl_add_vector` here as well? In theory the DNS SVCB parameter could be one or zero bytes, and `offset_end - 2` would result in an integer overflow, and potentially an infinite loop. "Luckily", `dissect_ech_echconfig` should throw an exception in that case.

While at it, can we remove the `ECHConfigList` tree?

Then we would turn:
```
            SvcParam: ech
                SvcParamKey: ech (5)
                SvcParamValue length: 71
                ECHConfigList length: 69
                ECHConfigList
                    ECHConfig: cloudflare-ech.com
                        Version: 0xfe0d
                        <etc>
                    ECHConfig: cloudflare-ech.com
                        Version: 0xfe0d
                        <etc>
```
into
```

            SvcParam: ech
                SvcParamKey: ech (5)
                SvcParamValue length: 71
                ECHConfigList length: 69
                ECHConfig: cloudflare-ech.com
                    Version: 0xfe0d
                    <etc>
                ECHConfig: cloudflare-ech.com
                    Version: 0xfe0d
                    <etc>
```
Since ECHConfig is already collapsible, I don't think we lose a lot by omitting the ECHConfigList container.

Likewise for the Retry Configs extension.
